Regulatory Transformation

Regulatory Transformation: navigating emerging risks, driving AI adoption and reducing regulatory burden

Regulators are facing a shifting operating environment as technology, markets, environmental pressures and societal expectations evolve faster than traditional regulatory frameworks. Fragmented data and limited intelligence continue to make risk prioritisation difficult.

There is a growing opportunity to use advanced analytics to better target regulatory effort. Many regulators are still working to integrate data across systems, uplift analytical capability and embed insights into everyday decision-making.

AI adoption is also becoming a core regulatory transformation issue. Regulators are seeking to balance opportunities for automation and improved risk identification with the need to manage governance, transparency, bias, legal risk, privacy and public confidence.

At the same time, governments are under pressure to reduce red tape, make faster decisions and manage fiscal constraints. This is driving interest in regulatory consolidation, shared-service models and more consistent approaches to regulatory delivery, while maintaining fairness and strong outcomes.

Regulation Hub Intelligence Brief

AI Brief 378 articles across 8 categories

The NDIS reform agenda dominates this fortnight across three interlocked pressure points: integrity and fraud risk inside NDIA, contested legislative passage of the participant-exit bill, and a mandatory provider registration wave now in motion. The AFP charge against an NDIA employee over an alleged $5 million fraud plot exposes material internal control gaps within the Agency and opens an immediate assurance pitch to NDIA leadership before the story hardens into a governance crisis. The Commonwealth's plan to exit 240,000 participants has drawn a joint states-and-territories warning that mainstream services cannot absorb the load; the Grattan Institute and the government's own parliamentary committee have simultaneously labelled the reforms blunt, inequitable, and likely to cause harm, while Coalition and Greens are signalling they may combine to slow the bill — creating a protracted transition environment that sustains advisory demand regardless of outcome. The NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission's concurrent activation of mandatory registration and SIL transition pathways generates a second, provider-side compliance wave that is proceeding independently of parliamentary risk. In aged care, Inside Ageing's survey data confirming providers are struggling with the new Aged Care Act's operational complexity, combined with the Medical Republic's call for an urgent overhaul of GP care in residential settings, signals stalled post-royal-commission implementation as an active engagement frontier. The Mandarin's coverage of shared registration infrastructure for the care economy points to a cross-sector digital program where KPMG's technology and managed-services bench should be pre-positioning now. BD effort this fortnight should concentrate on NDIA fraud assurance, NDIS transition architecture with Commonwealth and state government clients, and Aged Care Act implementation readiness for large residential providers.

Cross-category themes

Across all categories, a consistent pattern of simultaneous legislative reform and sharpened enforcement — spanning ACCC, ASIC, AUSTRAC, APRA, TEQSA, CASA and state regulators — is materially expanding compliance exposure and accelerating the need for clients to rebuild risk frameworks, internal controls, and governance structures ahead of implementation deadlines. For KPMG advisory practices, the most significant cross-cutting opportunity lies at the intersection of AML/Tranche 2 readiness, penalty risk uplift, and sector-specific regulatory modernisation, while the ASIC investigation into KPMG itself demands immediate internal conflict-management and independence protocols.

AI Brief50 articles

ASIC's simultaneous release of updated advertising guidance for financial products and a refreshed financial complaints data dashboard signals a dual enforcement-and-transparency push that will drive urgent compliance reviews across ADIs, super funds, and licensees — creating immediate demand for gap-analysis and remediation advisory. APRA's recognition of the super-sector accountability reform agenda (centred on superannuation transparency and member outcomes) reinforces a sustained regulatory investment cycle in governance uplift for large funds, supporting pitches for assurance, benchmarking, and governance-framework engagements. Enforcement of financial-reporting obligations — evidenced by the $596k in infringement notices against Zara, H&M and Sephora brands — raises the regulatory cost of non-compliance and sharpens appetite for proactive reporting-quality reviews among mid-market retail and financial-services clients. The proposed withdrawal of financial-reporting relief for uncontactable members further tightens super-fund operational obligations, pointing to a second wave of member-data remediation work in the coming quarter.

Implications for KPMGPartners should use the ASIC advertising guidance update as a door-opener with heads of compliance across banking and wealth clients this fortnight — a rapid gap-analysis offering tied to the revised guidance is immediately pitchable. The APRA super accountability signal warrants a coordinated approach between the Financial Services and People & Change teams to position governance and accountability framework engagements ahead of the next APRA heat-map cycle.

Northern Territory

AI Brief49 articles

NT WorkSafe has escalated WHS enforcement significantly, bringing charges against the NT Health Department over a patient death involving aerosol can inhalation at Darwin Hospital, as well as separate charges against an Aboriginal corporation over a fatal ute rollover and an outback arts centre following a worker fatality — signalling a clear prosecutorial shift toward accountability across both public-sector and community entities. A damning independent report citing 'persistent and serious systemic failings' in child protection has reinforced the NT Government's reform agenda, attracting federal intervention from Prime Minister Albanese and creating regulatory advisory opportunities around implementation compliance for First Nations-facing service providers. NT consumer protection regulators levied $38,000 in fines against service stations for fuel overcharging at the bowser, while Commonwealth Border Force disrupted a multi-million-dollar illicit tobacco operation in the NT, highlighting active multi-agency enforcement across consumer and excise compliance. These developments collectively signal heightened regulatory risk for NT-operating organisations in WHS, child safety, and consumer law, with cross-jurisdictional federal engagement adding complexity to reform timelines.

State-gov priorities

Cited strategic priorities across all 9 jurisdictions, refreshed bi-annually. Every source URL is .gov.au.

Housing supply dominates as the single strongest cross-jurisdiction theme, with every state and territory committing to measurable dwelling targets — from ACT's 30,000 homes by 2030 and Tasmania's 10,000 affordable homes by 2032 through to Victoria's 2.24 million by 2051 and Queensland's 1 million by 2046 — creating a sustained pipeline of planning reform, infrastructure sequencing, and social housing delivery work. Paired with this is a near-universal infrastructure investment push, with ACT, NSW, SA, WA, and Tasmania all operating or refreshing long-term infrastructure strategies, and NSW and ACT committing to major transit expansion, signalling sustained demand for business case development, program assurance, and delivery governance support. Industrial and manufacturing policy has emerged as a second tier of alignment: the Commonwealth's Future Made in Australia, WA's Made in WA fund, NSW's state-owned manufacturing push, SA's State Prosperity Project, and NT's economic strategy all reflect a deliberate shift toward onshore capability and supply chain resilience, with KPMG well-placed to offer investment facilitation, economic modelling, and industry policy design. Energy transition shows strong convergence in ambition but divergence in instrument — SA and Tasmania are pursuing aggressive renewable and hydrogen targets anchored to export and grid leadership, ACT is integrating net zero into budget frameworks, while NT and Queensland are simultaneously doubling down on resources extraction (mining, LNG, the QRIDP), creating a genuine policy tension where KPMG can offer independent stakeholder consultation and transition strategy work for both incumbent and emerging industries. Public safety and justice reform is a quieter but consistent thread, with NT's crime reduction strategy, Queensland's youth justice overhaul, and NSW's domestic violence reforms all representing politically charged program delivery contexts where implementation assurance and community consultation capability are high-value propositions. The Commonwealth's APS Reform Agenda and Victoria's Royal Commission mental health implementation round out a pattern of large, multi-year machinery-of-government transformations that require sustained capability uplift — workforce design, change management, and performance monitoring — areas where KPMG's PEPI practice holds strong positioning across multiple jurisdictions simultaneously.

Last refreshed 2026-05-20. Bi-annual schedule; source URLs verified to .gov.au.

Commonwealth

  • Future Made in Australia
    The Treasury / Department of Industry, Science and Resources 2024-2034 (10-year, $22.7B package)
    Program design, sector assessment frameworks, investment mandate design, industry consultation, economic modelling, community benefit evaluation
    Source (2024-05-14)
  • Strengthening Medicare
    Department of Health, Disability and Ageing 2023-2027 (reform rolling); Budget 2025-26 expansion from Nov 2025
    Primary care reform evaluation, Urgent Care Clinic rollout support, workforce modelling, digital health implementation, Medicare integrity assurance
    Source (2024-05-14)
  • 2024 National Defence Strategy and Integrated Investment Program
    Department of Defence 2024-2034 ($330B Integrated Investment Program to 2033-34)
    Capability program assurance, workforce strategy, sovereign industrial capability priorities, AUKUS implementation support, capability reviews
    Source (2024-04-17)
  • APS Reform Agenda
    Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet / Australian Public Service Commission 2022-ongoing (4 pillars, 59 initiatives; Public Service Amendment Act 2024 enacted)
    Integrity and capability reviews, workforce strategy, stewardship framework design, data & digital workforce planning, contractor-to-APS conversion support
    Source (2024-12-01)
  • Working for Women: A Strategy for Gender Equality
    Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (Office for Women) 2024-2034 (10-year strategy)
    Gender impact analysis, workplace gender equality evaluation, Government Board appointment strategy support, pay-gap economic modelling, consultation design
    Source (2024-03-07)
  • Aged Care reform – transition to Support at Home
    Department of Health, Disability and Ageing Aged Care Act 2024 commenced 1 Nov 2025; CHSP transition to Support at Home by 1 Jul 2027
    Provider transition support, data and digital strategy implementation, workforce modelling, single assessment system evaluation, consumer journey design
    Source (2024-07-01)

New South Wales

  • Safe Staffing Levels in NSW public hospitals
    NSW Ministry of Health Phase one early 2024; full rollout 2,480 FTE nurses/midwives by June 2027
    Workforce modelling, implementation assurance, change management support, clinical governance advisory, rostering system review
    Source (2024-03-11)
  • Transport Oriented Development Program (TOD)
    Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure TOD planning controls commenced 13 May 2024; 15-year horizon; 170,000+ homes
    Precinct planning, inclusionary zoning advisory, infrastructure funding strategy, development feasibility, stakeholder consultation
    Source (2024-05-13)
  • Sydney Metro – Western Sydney Airport and Sydney Metro West
    Transport for NSW / Sydney Metro Western Sydney Airport line opens 2026; Metro West completion by 2032; network to 46 stations by 2030
    Program assurance, capability reviews, cost estimation reviews, land use integration, precinct economic analysis
    Source (2024-06-01)
  • Bringing back manufacturing to NSW (state-owned energy and rollingstock)
    Cabinet Office / Treasury NSW / Transport for NSW 2023-2027+ (current Parliament)
    Industrial strategy advisory, local content analysis, state-owned corporation establishment, procurement strategy, workforce development
    Source (2024-09-01)
  • NSW Budget 2025-26 priorities (essential services + diversified economy)
    NSW Treasury 2025-26 forward estimates to 2028-29
    Fiscal strategy advisory, expenditure review, program evaluation, revenue analysis, investment prioritisation
    Source (2025-06-24)
  • Safer Pathway – domestic and family violence response
    Department of Communities and Justice Statewide rollout ongoing; DFV reforms 2024-ongoing
    Service design, outcomes evaluation, risk assessment framework review, cross-agency data sharing advisory, program logic review
    Source (2024-01-01)

Victoria

  • Victoria's Housing Statement – The Decade Ahead 2024-2034
    Department of Transport and Planning 2024-2034 (800,000 homes / 80,000 per year target)
    Planning reform advisory, activity centre masterplans, affordable housing economics, surplus land unlocking, stakeholder consultation, LGA target negotiations
    Source (2023-09-20)
  • Plan for Victoria (long-term plan to 2051)
    Department of Transport and Planning Released Feb 2025; horizon to 2051 (2.24 million homes target)
    LGA housing target analysis, settlement pattern modelling, sustainability and climate policy integration, First Peoples self-determination in planning, infrastructure sequencing
    Source (2025-02-01)
  • Mental Health and Wellbeing reform (Royal Commission implementation)
    Department of Health 2021-2031 (decade of reform); Statewide Service and Capital Plan 2024-2037
    Service design, capital planning, workforce strategy, outcomes evaluation, lived experience engagement design, Mental Health Levy economic analysis
    Source (2024-07-01)
  • Treaty for Victoria / First Peoples' self-determination
    First Peoples – State Relations Statewide Treaty Bill 2025 introduced; negotiations ongoing
    Closing the Gap accountability framework design, service commissioning transition, policy impact analysis, governance advisory for new representative body
    Source (2025-02-01)
  • Breakthrough Victoria Fund – research and innovation commercialisation
    Department of Jobs, Skills, Industry and Regions 2020-2030 ($2B 10-year fund; $1.3B co-investment leveraged by 2024)
    Commercialisation strategy, innovation ecosystem review, investment thesis advisory, co-investment deal structuring, industry sector analysis
    Source (2024-06-30)

Queensland

  • Making Queensland Safer – adult crime, adult time youth justice reform
    Department of Youth Justice and Victim Support (renamed 1 Nov 2024) Making Queensland Safer Act 2024 assented 13 Dec 2024; Queensland Youth Justice Strategy 2024-2028
    Program logic review, early intervention evaluation, victim advocacy service design, circuit breaker sentencing assurance, regional reset program evaluation
    Source (2024-08-01)
  • Homes for Queenslanders housing plan
    Department of Housing and Public Works 2024-2046 (1 million new homes by 2046; 53,500 social homes)
    Housing target modelling, modular housing economics, social housing procurement, church/charity land strategy, planning reform advisory
    Source (2024-02-14)
  • A Fresh Start – cost-of-living and tax relief
    Queensland Treasury 100 Day Plan completed early 2025; ongoing measures 2024-2028
    Revenue impact modelling, cost-of-living measure evaluation, payroll tax analysis, first home buyer stamp duty modelling
    Source (2025-02-01)
  • Queensland Resources Industry Development Plan (QRIDP)
    Department of Natural Resources and Mines, Manufacturing and Regional and Rural Development 2022-2052 (30-year vision; living document)
